purpose: CopyText shows one code value (a CSS custom property, a utility class, a CNAME, a key ID, a one-line command) in monospace inside a quiet bordered box, with an always-visible `CopyButton` at its inline end that copies the value. It composes `CopyButton` for the clipboard write, the copied confirmation, the live announcement and the manual-copy fallback, so it re-implements none of them. Unlike `CopyButton` (icon only, no visible value) and `TableCellId` (an identifier laid out for a table cell), CopyText is the inline "show this value and let me copy it" pattern for prose, key/value lists, token tables and cards.
useWhen: Show a short code value the reader will paste elsewhere, next to its label: a design token (`--spacing-2xl`), a class (`p-(--spacing-2xl)`), a CNAME, an API key ID, a one-line CLI command.
Token tables, key/value rows, setup steps and cards outside a data table.
avoidWhen: The value is not shown, only copied → use `copy-button`.
An identifier inside a data table cell → use `table-cell-id`.
A multi-line snippet or a block of code → use `code-block`.
A secret that must stay masked until revealed → use `password` (read-only) with a `copy-button`.
related: `copy-button` — the control CopyText composes; use it alone when the value is not displayed.
`table-cell-id` — the same idea laid out for a table cell (fills the cell, outline button).
`code-block` — multi-line code with its own copy control.
`kbd` — keycaps for shortcuts, not copyable values.
bestPractices: Pass the exact text in `value`; CopyText shows and copies the same string.
Keep values to one line. A long value truncates with an ellipsis; the full value stays in the `title`, in the accessible name of the copy button and in the clipboard.
Pass `ariaLabel` when the value alone does not say what it is (`Copy CNAME`); the default reads `Copy {value}`.
Listen to `copy` for analytics or a toast; it fires only after the clipboard write succeeds.
Use `size="small"` in dense tables and lists.
